name: Circadian Architectural Regulation via Non-Visual Photoreception
mechanism_chain_provenance: INHERITED from Document 34 (L2) — causal chain structure preserved at 'established' maturity; quantitative parameters newly established in LIGHT-I

mechanism_chain.description: Architectural design decisions → spectral power distribution + corneal melanopic irradiance (m-EDI)

data.finding: For a D65 reference illuminant (6500K), 1 photopic lux ≈ 0.9 m-lux mEDI; for warm white LED (2700K), 1 photopic lux ≈ 0.31 m-lux mEDI
data.effect: 3:1 ratio in melanopic content between warm and cool sources at same photopic illuminance

data.finding: Real-world daytime melanopic exposures in conventional office buildings typically fall in 10-50 m-lux range, substantially below laboratory thresholds
data.paradigm: Field dosimetry with calibrated light-at-eye sensors
data.effect: Office workers in highest-quartile averaged ~75 m-lux during peak morning hours
data.design: Cross-sectional field study with objective measurement

justification.backing: The translation from architectural design parameters to corneal melanopic irradiance rests on CIE S 026:2018 standardized conversion factors that account for light source spectral power distribution. Figueiro's field data establish what real buildings actually deliver. The combined evidence provides both the conversion methodology and the empirical validation.
justification.qualifier: Conversion factors depend on spectral power distribution; values given assume specific source types. Real building delivery varies substantially with occupant position, gaze direction, shading state, and furniture configuration.
justification.rebuttal: This step would fail if: (a) the CIE S 026 melanopic weighting function does not accurately capture the spectral sensitivity of human ipRGCs; (b) occupant behavior systematically modifies light exposure in ways not captured by static architectural calculations.

mechanism_chain.description: → M1 ipRGC melanopsin phototransduction (Gq/11 → PLCβ4 → IP3/DAG → TRP channel depolarization)

data.finding: Melanopsin is a bistable opsin using Gq/11 signaling to activate PLCβ4 and open TRPC6/7 channels; peak sensitivity ~480nm
data.effect: Sustained depolarization response with minutes-scale integration

data.finding: M1 ipRGCs have highest melanopsin density among subtypes and provide primary SCN-projecting population
data.effect: M1 cells specifically innervate SCN core

justification.backing: The molecular cascade from melanopsin activation through Gq/11 signaling to TRP channel opening is well-characterized in molecular neuroscience. This is a constitutive biochemical relationship established through multiple converging techniques.
justification.qualifier: The molecular mechanism is established in animal models; human ipRGCs are presumed homologous but direct human retinal physiology data is limited. The threshold for activation varies with temporal integration.
justification.rebuttal: This step would fail if: (a) human melanopsin signaling differs substantially from mouse; (b) other opsins (cone opsins, rhodopsin) contribute substantially to the circadian signal in ways not captured by melanopic weighting.

mechanism_chain.description: → M1 axon projection via retinohypothalamic tract → glutamate + PACAP co-release at SCN core

data.finding: M1 ipRGC axons project monosynaptically to SCN via retinohypothalamic tract (RHT); synapses release both glutamate and PACAP

justification.backing: The RHT is a well-characterized neural pathway. The co-transmission of glutamate (fast) and PACAP (slow/sustained) at SCN synapses provides both immediate and sustained signaling for circadian photoentrainment.
justification.qualifier: Established in rodent models; human RHT presumed homologous. PACAP signaling may modulate sensitivity in ways not fully characterized.
justification.rebuttal: This step would fail if: (a) human RHT has different projection patterns; (b) other retinal cell types contribute significantly to SCN input.

mechanism_chain.description: → SCN core (retinorecipient shell): NMDA-R + PAC1-R → CREB phosphorylation → Per1/Per2 transcription (phase-shifting signal)

data.finding: Light-induced phase shifts require CREB phosphorylation and Per1/Per2 gene induction in SCN; blocking NMDA-R or PAC1-R blocks phase shifting
data.source: Travnickova-Bendova et al. (2002); Albrecht et al. (2001)
data.paradigm: Molecular biology with gene knockout and pharmacology
data.effect: Per1/Per2 induction within 30-60 minutes of light exposure

data.finding: The phase response curve (PRC) maps light timing to phase shift direction and magnitude; maximum shifts ~1.5-2h
data.source: Kronauer et al. (1999); Czeisler et al. (1989)
data.effect: PRC with ~2h maximum shift at optimal circadian phase

justification.backing: The molecular clock mechanism is one of the most thoroughly characterized biological oscillator systems. The CREB-Per pathway connects light input to core clock gene expression. The phase response curve integrates molecular and behavioral levels.
justification.qualifier: The molecular cascade operates on gene expression timescales (hours); architectural effects must consider integration over the full morning period. Individual chronotype modulates PRC timing.
justification.rebuttal: This step would fail if: (a) light-induced Per gene expression does not translate to functional phase shifts in humans; (b) non-photic zeitgebers (feeding, activity) dominate over photic input in real-world conditions.

mechanism_chain.description: → SCN shell (non-retinorecipient): VIP interneuron synchronization of core-to-shell coupling → coherent population oscillator

data.finding: SCN network coupling via VIP-VPAC2 signaling synchronizes individual cellular oscillators into coherent population rhythm
data.source: Welsh et al. (2010); Aton et al. (2005)
data.effect: Loss of VIP signaling desynchronizes SCN population

justification.backing: The SCN is not a single clock but a network of coupled oscillators. VIP interneurons provide the coupling signal that maintains population coherence. This network property determines the robustness and stability of the circadian output.
justification.qualifier: SCN network dynamics are characterized in vitro and in animal models; human SCN is presumed similar but direct evidence is limited.
justification.rebuttal: This step would fail if: (a) human SCN uses different coupling mechanisms; (b) individual cellular heterogeneity is larger than network coupling can overcome.

mechanism_chain.description: → SCN output: PVN → superior cervical ganglion → pineal (NE → β-AR → melatonin synthesis suppression/release timing)

data.finding: SCN polysynaptic output to pineal via PVN and sympathetic system controls melatonin synthesis; light acutely suppresses melatonin via this pathway
data.effect: Melatonin rhythm phase-locked to SCN; acute suppression within 30 min of bright light

data.finding: Melatonin suppression threshold approximately 30-50 m-lux mEDI during evening; 50% suppression achievable with moderate room light
data.effect: Dose-dependent suppression; threshold ~30 m-lux in evening sensitivity window

justification.backing: The SCN-pineal pathway is one of the most thoroughly characterized neuroendocrine axes. Melatonin is a reliable circadian marker and is directly modulated by light via this pathway. The suppression threshold is well-characterized.
justification.qualifier: Melatonin suppression and phase shifting are distinct phenomena with different thresholds (Arendt). Acute suppression threshold (~30 m-lux) is lower than phase-shifting threshold (~75-100 m-lux). Architectural recommendations must distinguish these.
justification.rebuttal: This step would fail if: (a) melatonin suppression has no functional consequence for sleep or circadian phase; (b) pineal melatonin production is regulated by non-photic factors that dominate over light input.

mechanism_chain.description: → SCN output: corticotrophin-releasing hormone rhythm → HPA cortisol awakening response timing

data.finding: The cortisol awakening response (CAR) is phase-locked to the SCN oscillator and represents a key physiological marker of circadian alignment
data.effect: CAR timing tracks circadian phase; blunted CAR indicates misalignment

justification.backing: The HPA axis is modulated by SCN output. The cortisol awakening response provides a functional marker of circadian alignment with direct consequences for morning alertness and metabolic function.
justification.qualifier: The CAR-delay coefficient (0.25h delay per 1h phase shift) is derived from shift-work studies; direct architectural measurement is absent. This is flagged as THEORETICAL_DEFAULT.
justification.rebuttal: This step would fail if: (a) CAR timing is dominated by sleep timing rather than circadian phase; (b) the HPA axis adapts to chronic misalignment such that CAR recovers despite persistent phase delay.

mechanism_chain.description: → Aligned melatonin + cortisol rhythms → sleep architecture quality + daytime alertness + metabolic function

data.finding: Workers with higher morning circadian stimulus (CS > 0.3) showed better sleep quality and mood than those with lower exposure (CS < 0.15)
data.paradigm: Field study with light dosimetry and outcomes
data.effect: d ≈ 0.30 on Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index

data.finding: Circadian misalignment from shift work is associated with metabolic syndrome, cognitive impairment, and increased disease risk
data.source: Scheer et al. (2009); Cho et al. (2000)
data.effect: Multiple adverse outcomes from chronic misalignment

justification.backing: The health consequences of circadian alignment are supported by both field studies in occupied buildings and laboratory/epidemiological studies of misalignment. The architectural translation is more uncertain than the basic physiology.
justification.qualifier: Effect sizes in field studies (d ≈ 0.30) are modest and subject to confounding. Individual variation in chronotype and sleep need modulates the relationship between architectural light and outcomes.
justification.rebuttal: This step would fail if: (a) the field study correlations are confounded by socioeconomic or job type differences; (b) individual chronotype differences are larger than architectural effects; (c) behavioral adaptation eliminates the architectural influence.

mechanism_chain.description: → Misaligned rhythms (insufficient daytime melanopic irradiance) → persistent temporal PE → allostatic load via T7 pathway

data.finding: Circadian misalignment produces inflammatory markers, metabolic dysregulation, and cognitive impairment consistent with allostatic load model
data.paradigm: Laboratory misalignment and allostatic load framework
data.effect: Multiple physiological markers of stress accumulation

justification.backing: The allostatic load framework (McEwen) provides the theoretical bridge connecting circadian misalignment to cumulative physiological wear. Persistent temporal prediction error from misalignment is conceptualized as a continuous body-budget mismatch that accumulates into allostatic load.
justification.qualifier: The link between circadian misalignment and allostatic load is theoretical. The 'temporal PE' framing derives from predictive processing theory; direct measurement of temporal PE is not available. This connection to T7 pathway is a theoretical integration.
justification.rebuttal: This step would fail if: (a) the body adapts to chronic misalignment such that PE diminishes over time; (b) behavioral compensation (caffeine, naps, weekend recovery) eliminates the allostatic accumulation; (c) the allostatic load concept does not accurately capture the physiological consequences.

advance_direction.note: Advance direction (morning light → phase advance). Maximum PRC advance region ≈ 1.5–2.0h for a single 3-hour 100 m-lux pulse; distributed architectural exposure produces approximately 0.85h/day on average.
advance_direction.source: Kronauer et al. (1999); Czeisler et al. (1989)

delay_direction.note: Delay direction (evening light → phase delay). Intrinsically faster than advance; consistent with free-running period > 24h.

circadian_entrainment.architectural_implication: A new occupant entering a building with substantially different light timing than their prior environment will require 3–10 days to re-entrain, depending on the magnitude of the phase difference and the quality of the architectural circadian stimulus.

hpa_axis_activation.note: Each hour of accumulated circadian phase delay (from evening light exposure or insufficient morning light) delays the cortisol awakening response (CAR) peak by approximately 0.25 hours. CAR blunting has direct cognitive consequence: peak alertness delayed, morning performance impaired.
hpa_axis_activation.source: Scheer et al. (2009); Figueiro et al. (2017) — indirect derivation
hpa_axis_activation.flag: THEORETICAL_DEFAULT — the 0.25 coefficient is derived from the relationship between circadian phase delay and CAR timing in shift-work studies; direct architectural measurement is absent

temporal_rhythm.note: Minimum morning CS required for measurable improvements in sleep quality and mood in office field studies. CS 0.3 is Figueiro's recommended target; 0.23 is the minimum showing statistically significant effect in her data.
temporal_rhythm.conversion_note: CS 0.23 ≈ 65 m-lux mEDI for cool-white LED (4000K); ≈ 105 m-lux for warm-white (2700K). Source CCT matters substantially.

building_types: priority: hospitals, eldercare, schools, shift-work facilities
ie_dpt_interaction: T_IE_001 (Activity-Frame Complexity Retuning) — explicit awareness of circadian health benefits from daylight modulates willingness to seek window-adjacent workstations and to use shading controls appropriately
panel_reasoning_excerpt:
## Panel Charge

Roger Ulrich's finding that hospital patients with a view of trees recovered faster than those with a view of a brick wall (Ulrich, 1984, ~7,000 citations) is the single most cited study in the architecture-wellbeing literature. Yet the project has no dedicated template for the VIEW mechanism. Ulrich's finding is referenced by T1 (fractal fluency of natural scenes), the Biophilia reduction (Doc 19), SC2 (isovist as visual prediction horizon), and T25 (directed attention and ART). But the specific mechanism — how the CONTENT of what is visible through a window affects the occupant — has not been formalized as a template.

The gap is not merely that Ulrich is uncited but that the VIEW mechanism involves a convergence of multiple existing templates that has not been made explicit: a window view of nature simultaneously engages fractal fluency (T1), prospect/refuge balance (T5/SC2), attention restoration (T25/ART), circadian light entrainment (L2), dynamic temporal variation (L5), and ecological familiarity (MAT4's convergence principle applied to visual scenes). The view is a multi-channel stimulus, and the convergence is what makes it powerful.

The panel is charged with producing 1–2 templates covering: (a) view content as a PE mechanism — how the brain generates predictions about what should be visible from a window and how different view contents (nature, urban, wall, sky) modulate PE, attention restoration, and affect, and (b) the window as a multi-channel environmental mediator — how windows provide not just a view but daylight (L2/L3), temporal information (L5), acoustic connection, and olfactory access to the outdoors. These must connect to T1 (fractal fluency), T25 (directed attention/ART), T29 (allostatic regulation), L2/L3 (circadian/daylight), SC2 (isovist), and the Biophilia reduction (Doc 19).

---

cross_template_interactions.IC2: Body Budget Prediction — primary interaction: circadian alignment is the temporal backbone of the interoceptive body-budget model. The cortisol awakening response, temperature rhythm, and melatonin cycle collectively constitute the predictive scaffold for body-budget regulation across the day. Misalignment produces persistent body-budget prediction errors that accumulate into allostatic load via T6 and T7.
cross_template_interactions.AX4: Perceived Control — operable shading, task lighting, and window access give occupants the ability to modulate their circadian light dose. High AX4 reduces allostatic cost of circadian misalignment by allowing active correction.
